subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests

question: Should Microsoft Teams file uploads use a transfer-aware deadline, or should maintainers explicitly accept a fixed five-minute cutoff for all supported payload sizes?
rationale: Current main supports files up to 100 MiB and has no transfer cutoff; choosing the minimum supported upload rate is a compatibility decision that code review cannot infer safely.

options.title: Require transfer-aware deadline
options.body: Scale the deadline from payload size with a conservative documented minimum rate, while retaining a floor for smaller transfers.

options.title: Accept five-minute cutoff
options.body: Keep the fixed deadline and explicitly accept that valid slower uploads can fail and require retry.

recommendation.title: Require transfer-aware deadline
recommendation.body: Scale the deadline from payload size with a conservative documented minimum rate, while retaining a floor for smaller transfers.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced the shared Microsoft Teams timeout owner that should define the final policy used by both upload paths.
